text:
There is diluted moon beneath your eyes,

and the scent of jasmine, and sad singing;

nostalgia fell asleep in them,

dissolved in the pearls of a sweet weeping...


When you cry, your pure tears sing

the sacred hymns that Eros formed,

and in your arcane dark pupils there are

the deep mysteries Apollo sang.


Dreams faint on their sad satins,

which silently resemble pale sunsets...

pale sunsets of smiling illusion...


While their bonfires light your lips

and the shadows beneath your eyes fasten to your face

the pale blue lily of their heart...




Note: Concha Urquiza wrote this poem when she was 12 years old.

translation.title: There Is Diluted Moon Beneath Your Eyes...
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the youthful, ornate imagery and keeps the biographical note.
